items.title: 52240_Frank _Machito_ Grillo oral history interview
items.q: in those days, Roberto, Bobby Rodriguez, was playing with us.

ctx.x: He made the arrangement and we play it, but naturally, he didn't have the meter, the correct meter that we used. Clavé, like we use, and the bass syncopation was missing, one or two notes that was the ones to complete the meter; so Rene, Mario and myself we wrote that. Bam, bam, bin bin, bam bam bin bin, pang, pang, ping, pang pa. They wrote pang pang ping ping pang pa, incomplete. It was nice, but for - to us is something was missing, so in those days, Roberto, Bobby Rodriguez, was playing with us. A good…

to the house. His uncle was a tremendous bass player with the Cuarteto Caney, so he had all that thing that you just can't avoid to have because you grew up with it. He had the education of that particular syncopation on the bass, so for him it was very easy to put whatever was lacked that particular part of the bass.
